lines.text: You can recognise a hydrocarbon by checking its elements, regardless of its shape or size.
A hydrocarbon is a compound made up of carbon and hydrogen atoms only. A formula containing oxygen, nitrogen or a halogen is not a hydrocarbon, even if most atoms are carbon and hydrogen.
This definition identifies alkanes and alkenes as hydrocarbons, but excludes alcohols and carboxylic acids.
Hydrocarbon, carbon and hydrogen atoms only. Any other element excludes the compound.
Why is ethanol not a hydrocarbon even though it contains carbon and hydrogen?
A molecule can be organic without possessing a characteristic functional group.

Alkanes are simple, saturated hydrocarbons. They contain carbon and hydrogen only and have carbon carbon single bonds. Alkanes have no functional group, their C C and C H bonds form the hydrocarbon framework rather than a distinctive group such as C equals C or minus OH.
Compare an alkane with an alkene, the alkene has a C equals C functional group, which gives it characteristic addition reactions.
Alkanes are simple hydrocarbons. Alkanes have no functional group. Saturated means carbon carbon single bonds only.
Why does the presence of C H bonds not make an alkane a functional group compound?
Two compounds with similar carbon skeletons can react differently because one group changes.

A functional group is an atom or group of atoms responsible for characteristic chemical reactions. In the syllabus classes, the group dictates chemical properties and strongly influences physical properties. For example, an alkene contains C equals C, an alcohol minus OH, an aldehyde minus CHO, a ketone an internal C equals O, a carboxylic acid minus COOH, and an ester minus COO. Halogenoalkanes, acyl chlorides, amines, amides and nitriles have their own identifying groups. Members of one homologous series share the same functional group and characteristic reactions.
First identify the group, then use the formulas and naming rules for that class.
Functional groups give characteristic reactions. They influence physical and chemical properties. One homologous series shares one functional group.
Why do propene and propanol have different characteristic reactions?
One molecule can be represented in four ways, each representation answers a different question.

A general formula expresses the composition of a homologous series using n, such as C N H two n plus two for acyclic alkanes. A structural formula shows atom and group connectivity in condensed form. A displayed formula shows every atom and every bond, including O H. A skeletal formula shows the carbon framework as lines, each unlabelled end or vertex is carbon, and carbon bound hydrogens are omitted. Infer them by giving each carbon four bonds. Show heteroatoms and hydrogens on them. Interpret and use these representations for the syllabus classes, including hydrocarbons, halogenoalkanes, alcohols, carbonyl compounds, acids, esters, acyl chlorides, amines, amides and nitriles.
Count skeletal atoms and complete valencies before deducing a molecular formula.
General formula, series composition using n. Structural formula, condensed connectivity. Displayed formula, all atoms and bonds. Skeletal formula, carbon at each unlabelled end and vertex.
What must you add mentally when reading a skeletal formula?
A systematic name lets someone reconstruct a molecule's connectivity.

For simple aliphatic molecules up to six carbons, choose the longest parent chain containing the principal functional group. Number it to give that group the lowest locant. Use a carbon stem from meth through hex, indicate substituents and their positions, and give the class suffix, for example propan two ol or butanoic acid. Include a nitrile carbon in the parent count. For straight chain esters R C O O R prime, name the O bonded alkyl R prime first and the acid derived alkanoate part second, up to six carbons may occur in each ester part. This syllabus restricts esters and nitriles to straight chains.
The functional group identified first determines the suffix and often controls numbering.
Choose the parent chain containing the main group. Number for the lowest functional group locant. Ester, O bonded alkyl name, then alkanoate. Count nitrile carbon in its parent chain.
Which part of methyl propanoate supplies the word methyl?
A drawing tells you the actual atom count, a simplest ratio may hide that count.

Deduce a molecular formula by counting all atoms in a structural or displayed formula. In a skeletal formula, count every unlabelled end and vertex as carbon, then supply carbon bound hydrogens to complete carbon valency four, accounting for double or triple bonds. Include shown heteroatoms and their hydrogens. The molecular formula records actual numbers of atoms. The empirical formula gives the simplest whole number ratio, divide all molecular subscripts by their greatest common factor. For C four H eight O two this gives C two H four O.
A correct skeletal count is the input for both formulas, only the empirical formula is reduced.
Molecular formula, actual atom counts. Complete skeletal carbon valencies before counting H. Empirical formula, simplest whole number ratio.

Propane, C three H eight, is a member of the alkanes. Which statement about functional groups in propane is correct?

Alkanes are simple saturated hydrocarbons with no functional group, a functional group is a reactive grouping beyond the alkane framework of C C and C H single bonds. The claims that C H bonds or terminal methyl groups are functional groups mistake part of that framework for a functional group, and being saturated is the absence of a reactive grouping, not the presence of one.
Recall how the syllabus describes the alkanes.
A functional group is responsible for a compound's characteristic reactions.
List the kinds of bond present in propane and ask which of them makes it react characteristically.
Ethanoic acid, C H three C O O H, and methyl methanoate, H C O O C H three, both have molecular formula C two H four O two. Deduce which statement about their boiling points is correct.

Ethanoic acid is a carboxylic acid and methyl methanoate is an ester. Both contain polar bonds, but only ethanoic acid has an O H bond and can form hydrogen bonds between its own molecules. These stronger intermolecular attractions give ethanoic acid the higher boiling point. A shared molecular formula does not imply identical physical properties, so the claim that the boiling points must be the same is wrong. Methyl methanoate has no O H bond and cannot hydrogen bond to itself, so the claim that its ester group allows hydrogen bonding between its own molecules is wrong. The two compounds have the same molecular formula and therefore the same relative molecular mass, so the claim that methyl methanoate has the larger relative molecular mass is wrong.

thirteen point one Formulas, functional groups and the naming of organic compounds.
In one breath.

A hydrocarbon is made up of carbon and hydrogen atoms only. A functional group gives an organic family its characteristic properties, formulas and systematic names describe its atoms and connectivity.
Key ideas.

A hydrocarbon is a compound made up of carbon and hydrogen atoms only. Ethene qualifies, ethanol does not, because it also contains oxygen. Alkanes are simple saturated hydrocarbons with no functional group. Their carbon atoms are joined by single bonds. A functional group is the atom or group of atoms responsible for a compound's characteristic chemical reactions. It dictates chemical properties and strongly influences physical properties across a homologous series. An alkene has a C equals C group, an alcohol has minus OH, an aldehyde has minus CHO, a ketone has C equals O within a chain, a carboxylic acid has minus COOH. Other syllabus families include halogenoalkanes, esters, acyl chlorides, amines, amides and nitriles. The same carbon skeleton with a different group can behave very differently.

A general formula describes every member of a homologous series using n, for acyclic alkanes it is C N H two n plus two, and for monohydric saturated alcohols it is C N H two n plus two O. A structural formula shows how atoms and groups are connected, such as C H three C H two O H. A displayed formula shows every atom and every bond, including the O H bond, writing a condensed structural formula when a displayed formula is requested can lose a mark. A skeletal formula uses an unlabelled line end or vertex for each carbon. Carbon bound hydrogens are omitted, infer enough to give each neutral carbon four bonds. Heteroatoms and hydrogens attached to them are shown. These representations can describe the same molecule, they reveal different amounts of detail.
Method.

Interpret a formula, Count all labelled atoms and every skeletal line end and vertex. Complete each carbon's valency of four, including multiple bonds. Count hydrogen on O or N when shown. This gives the molecular formula, the actual number of each atom in one molecule.

Find an empirical formula, Divide every molecular subscript by their highest common factor. The empirical formula is the simplest whole number atom ratio. For C four H eight O two, divide by two to get C two H four O, do not reduce only some elements.

Name a simple aliphatic molecule, Choose the longest parent chain containing the main functional group. Use meth, eth, prop, but, pent or hex for one to six carbons. Number from the end that gives the principal functional group the lowest possible locant, then locate double bonds and substituents. State locants, prefixes and the appropriate suffix, such as minus ol, minus al, minus one, minus oic acid or minus nitrile. The nitrile carbon counts in the parent chain. For an ester R C O O R prime, name the alkyl group R prime attached to oxygen first, then the acid derived alkanoate R C O O, the carbonyl carbon belongs to the latter chain. Use straight chains for esters and nitriles in this syllabus, with up to six carbons in each ester part.

Figure, Numbering a branched chain from each end, the methyl group takes the lower locant, so the name is three methylhexane, source, nine seven zero one c13.1, p.9. Notice that both numberings are legitimate ways to count the six carbon parent chain, and that it is the branch position alone that decides between them, three beats four, so only three methylhexane is the systematic name, written without a space.
Worked example.

Name C H three C H two C O O C H three and deduce its molecular and empirical formulas. The group beyond the single bond oxygen is methyl, the acid derived chain including the carbonyl carbon has three carbons. The systematic name is methyl propanoate. Count four carbons, eight hydrogens and two oxygens, molecular formula C four H eight O two. Divide subscripts by two, empirical formula C two H four O.
Traps.

Trap, Treat the empirical formula as the molecular formula. Why it's wrong, A simplest ratio may represent several molecular sizes. Instead, Count actual atoms first, then reduce only for an empirical formula.
Trap, Count only corners and miss line ends in skeletal formulas. Why it's wrong, Both stand for carbons. Instead, Mark every end and vertex before adding hydrogens.
Trap, Reverse ester parts. Why it's wrong, The alkyl name comes from the group bonded to the single bond oxygen. Instead, Find C O O minus before naming either part.
Exam technique.

Define hydrocarbon with carbon and hydrogen atoms only. In deduce questions, show how skeletal valencies give the molecular formula and how the common factor gives the empirical formula. When asked for a displayed formula, draw every bond, especially O H. Check the parent chain and locants before finalising a systematic name.
